a: Metallic bonding involves a lattice of positive ions in a sea of electrons.
Intermolecular forces affect boiling points and solubility.
Hydrogen bonds are strong intermolecular attractions involving H with N/O/F.
Oxidation numbers help track electron transfer in reactions.
Titration finds concentration by reacting with a known solution.
Reaction rate depends on concentration, temperature, and catalysts.
Activation energy is the energy barrier to start a reaction.
Enthalpy changes measure heat at constant pressure.
Entropy relates to dispersal of energy and matter.
Gibbs free energy predicts spontaneity under constant T and P.
